title: Docker Multilang: One Compose File, Three Runtimes

cover.alt: Conceptual three-part system with distinct API, worker, and web runtime structures on a shared network base.

figures.title: Three runtimes with separate jobs
figures.summary: Compose groups the services, while each runtime keeps its own purpose and build context.

items.label: Node API
items.detail: Returns random and sorted-number data through its HTTP routes.

items.label: Python worker
items.detail: Calls the API by its service name and logs the returned arrays.

items.label: Nginx web
items.detail: Serves the static page the browser uses to request data.

figures.caption: The roles are taken from the supplied lab code, not a claim about a larger production architecture.

figures.title: Check the boundaries between services
figures.summary: Most of the documented failures occur where one environment or process meets another.

items.label: Build inputs
items.detail: Confirm the lockfile exists before the Dockerfile copies it.

items.label: Browser origin
items.detail: Check whether a direct API call needs CORS handling or a same-origin proxy.

items.label: Host ports
items.detail: Check for an existing process using the mapped port.

items.label: Readiness
items.detail: Distinguish a started container from an API ready to accept the worker’s request.

figures.caption: Failure points described in the article. Reported build-time improvements are not reproduced as benchmark graphics.
